spec.prompt: Exterior in orbit, bright daylight. The Voskhod-2 spacecraft (third reference) is in the upper right of the frame: its long pale fabric Volga airlock cylinder sticks out from the ball-shaped cabin toward the camera-left, its outer end open, the round metal rim and the hinged hatch lid swung open beside it. A single thin white tether, about five metres long, runs from the rim of the airlock mouth to the waist of the cosmonaut Alexei Leonov (face and suit exactly as in the first two reference images), who floats alone in his white Berkut suit with its flat white backpack. He pulls himself back toward the ship along the tether, hand over hand: his right glove grips the tether and pulls, his left glove reaches past it, grips and pulls, again and again, slow and heavy in his stiff, over-inflated suit, the slack tether gathering in loose loops behind him. He drifts steadily closer until the open airlock mouth is just in front of his helmet, then he stops and grips the metal rim with one glove. He does not enter the airlock. Nobody else is visible; nobody pulls on the tether from inside. The sunlit blue Earth with white clouds curves along the bottom of the frame, black sky above. One continuous shot, no cuts, camera beside him at a medium-wide distance, slowly following. Photorealistic, shot on 35mm film, IMAX documentary realism in the spirit of Apollo 11 (2019) and Gravity. Accurate 1965 Soviet hardware: the white Berkut spacesuit with rust-orange harness straps, a white helmet with red CCCP letters above the visor, Soviet markings only. Hard directional sunlight, deep black space, crisp silhouettes. No on-screen text, no captions.
